findings.title: Crash when checking Google Meet fallback with empty/null destinationCalendar
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. If `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array (which `handleNewBooking.ts` now explicitly produces via `: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError. The old code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and was safe. Any booking using Google Meet as location without a destination calendar will now fail with an unhandled exception instead of falling back to Cal Video. This should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent only ever writes to the first host's destination calendar, silently skipping other hosts
findings.body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (used by CalDAV/Apple calendar) filters the credential's calendar list with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the FIRST element of `event.destinationCalendar` — i.e. the main host's calendar. In the new multi-host flow, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over every destination calendar and calls `createEvent` with each host's own credential, but this service ignores both the `credentialId` argument and the `externalId` passed to `CalendarManager.createEvent`, and keeps filtering by the main host's `externalId`. For a secondary host's CalDAV account that filter matches nothing, so `Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(...)` is false, and the method returns a success result with a uid even though no event was created anywhere. A booking reference is then stored claiming the event exists on the secondary host's calendar when it does not. The service should filter by the destination calendar matching the current credential (or accept the externalId), not always the first array entry.

findings.title: Team member destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: For collective events the code builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, and later does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional-chained push is a no-op, and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded — so hosts who DO have destination calendars never receive calendar events, which is exactly the scenario this PR is meant to fix. The collective branch should initialize the array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`).

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match, leaving calendarId undefined
findings.body: In both `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317) the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since this branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined/empty, the `find` compares each calendar's externalId against null/undefined and can never match, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` and is passed as `calendarId` to the Google API call, which will fail. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Callers such as `CalendarManager.updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` pass `externalCalendarId: null` when the booking reference has none stored, so this path is reachable; the fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId instead of a find that can never succeed.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link to the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is `undefined`), the event is inserted into "primary" but the patch is issued with `calendarId: undefined`, which the Google client rejects — and since the promise is not awaited or caught, this surfaces as an unhandled rejection. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `referencesToCreate` changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. For non-calendar (video) results, the credentialId is now always written as `undefined`, whereas before it carried `result.credentialId`. Downstream, `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set and resolvable to a user credential; bookings created after this change will have video references without credentialId, so cancelling them will leave orphaned video meetings (e.g. Zoom/Teams links stay alive). Unless no video adapter populates `result.credentialId` (in which case the old code was equally broken), this is a data regression for new bookings.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose credentialId/externalCalendarId fallbacks
findings.body: In `updateLocation`, `referencesToCreate` now uses `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`, removing the previous fallbacks to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. However `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (whose results feed this) never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` — only `createEvent` does. So calendar references created via the edit-location flow (`editLocation.handler.ts` does `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`) are now always persisted with null `externalCalendarId` and null `credentialId`, whereas before they inherited them from the destination calendar. Subsequent updates/cancellations rely on these fields to target the correct calendar and credential, so location-edited bookings degrade to the legacy 'try every credential' behavior or fail to update the right event.

findings.title: externalId not forwarded when destination has no credentialId
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch for a destination calendar without a `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, while the credentialId branch correctly calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. Since `CalendarManager.createEvent` stores that argument as `result.externalId` which becomes `externalCalendarId` on the booking reference, references created through this branch now have `externalCalendarId: undefined` even though the destination calendar's externalId is known. Pass `destination.externalId` here as well so future updates/deletes can target the right calendar.

findings.title: loadUsers no longer selects user.organization for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` for the dynamic-user (no eventTypeId) path selects `...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true` but drops the previously selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. Any downstream code that reads `user.organization?.slug` on the organizer/users (e.g. for building org-aware booker URLs) will now silently get `undefined` for dynamic group bookings. The PR description only concerns destination calendars, so this looks like an accidental omission during the refactor; re-add the `organization` select unless it is provably unused.
